skills.title: Web requests and browser rendering
skills.definition: A URL identifies a resource; the browser requests it, interprets the response, builds internal trees, and renders pixels.

skills.title: Semantic document skeleton
skills.definition: A valid page separates metadata from visible content and uses landmarks that communicate each region's purpose.

skills.title: Nesting and the document tree
skills.definition: HTML elements form a rooted tree: every non-root node has one parent, and correct nesting preserves the intended hierarchy.

skills.title: Text, links, images, and paths
skills.definition: Content elements carry meaning, while relative and absolute paths determine how a browser locates linked resources.

skills.title: Lists, tables, and structured records
skills.definition: Choose lists for sequences and tables for genuinely two-dimensional relationships with explicit headers.

skills.title: Forms as input-output contracts
skills.definition: A form maps labeled user inputs to named values, applies constraints, and submits a predictable record.

skills.title: Accessible HTML and keyboard flow
skills.definition: Names, roles, relationships, focus order, and alternatives make the same structure perceivable without relying on sight or a pointer.

skills.title: Validation, debugging, and static publishing
skills.definition: Debug from document structure outward: validate markup, inspect paths, test interaction order, then verify the deployed response.

skills.title: Cascade, specificity, and inheritance
skills.definition: The winning declaration is determined by origin, importance, specificity, and source order; only inheritable properties flow from parent to child.

skills.title: Box model and predictable sizing
skills.definition: Rendered size is the sum of content, padding, border, and margin unless border-box sizing moves padding and border inside the declared dimensions.

skills.title: Selectors, combinators, and UI states
skills.definition: Selectors describe sets of nodes and relationships; narrowly target stable structure without encoding accidental nesting.

skills.title: Normal flow, display, and positioning
skills.definition: Normal flow places boxes in document order; positioning should change a box's reference relationship only when the design requires it.

skills.title: Flexbox axes and alignment
skills.definition: Flexbox distributes items along one main axis and aligns them along the cross axis under available-space constraints.

skills.title: Grid tracks and two-dimensional layout
skills.definition: Grid defines row and column tracks, then places items into cells or named regions while preserving explicit spatial relationships.

skills.title: Responsive constraints and media queries
skills.definition: Responsive design selects fluid defaults and introduces breakpoints where content constraints—not device names—stop being satisfied.

skills.title: Design tokens, accessibility, and CSS debugging
skills.definition: Reusable tokens keep visual relationships consistent; contrast, focus, zoom, and inspector checks protect usability across states.

skills.title: Values, types, and explicit conversion
skills.definition: A value has a type that determines valid operations; explicit conversion makes input assumptions visible and testable.

skills.title: Variables, expressions, and state
skills.definition: A variable names a current value, while an expression maps existing values to a new result without changing unrelated state.

skills.title: Boolean logic and branching
skills.definition: A branch partitions possible states by predicates; conditions must be mutually understood and boundary cases tested.

skills.title: Loops, counters, and invariants
skills.definition: A loop needs an initial state, continuation condition, update, and invariant that remains true after every iteration.

skills.title: Functions as input-output mappings
skills.definition: A function defines a reusable contract from parameters to a return value or documented effect, with scope limiting accidental dependencies.

skills.title: Arrays and sequence transformations
skills.definition: Arrays model ordered data; map, filter, find, and reduce express distinct transformations with predictable output shapes.

skills.title: Objects, records, and lookup
skills.definition: Objects group named fields into records; safe access and deliberate updates preserve the record's expected shape.

skills.title: DOM events and interface state
skills.definition: An event supplies input, a handler computes a state transition, and rendering makes the new state visible in the document tree.

skills.title: Asynchronous timelines and promises
skills.definition: A promise represents a future result; awaiting it orders dependent work without blocking unrelated browser tasks.

skills.title: Fetch and HTTP response handling
skills.definition: A network request is not complete at receipt: code must inspect status, parse the expected body, and handle transport and application failures separately.

skills.title: JSON contracts and defensive parsing
skills.definition: External JSON is untrusted structured data; validate required fields and types before allowing it to update application state.

skills.title: Failures, retries, and user-visible states
skills.definition: Loading, success, empty, and failure are distinct states; retries must be bounded and safe for the operation being repeated.

skills.title: Browser storage and data lifetime
skills.definition: Choose memory, session, or persistent storage by lifetime, sensitivity, capacity, and synchronization needs.

skills.title: Modules and dependency boundaries
skills.definition: Modules expose small public contracts and hide internal details, producing a directed dependency graph that is easier to test.

skills.title: Functional transformations and immutability
skills.definition: Non-mutating transformations create a new value from old state, making change histories and UI updates easier to reason about.

skills.title: API-driven application architecture
skills.definition: Separate transport, validation, domain state, and rendering so each layer has one responsibility and failures stay localized.

skills.title: Components, JSX, and render trees
skills.definition: A component maps inputs and current state to a declarative subtree; composition builds the full interface tree.

skills.title: Props, contracts, and composition
skills.definition: Props are read-only inputs; clear prop contracts and composition keep parent-child responsibilities explicit.

skills.title: State, identity, and render transitions
skills.definition: State belongs at the nearest common owner, and stable identity determines whether React preserves or replaces a component's state.

skills.title: Events, controlled forms, and reducers
skills.definition: User events become actions; controlled values or reducers make each transition from previous state to next state explicit.

skills.title: Effects and synchronized external systems
skills.definition: An effect synchronizes rendering with an external system and needs accurate dependencies plus cleanup for obsolete work.

skills.title: Routing and shared application state
skills.definition: Routes form a navigation graph; only genuinely shared state should move above local component boundaries.

skills.title: Testing, accessibility, and performance
skills.definition: Test observable behavior, measure before optimizing, and preserve accessible names, focus, and feedback across every state.

skills.title: Build, deployment, and maintainable architecture
skills.definition: A deployable frontend has reproducible builds, environment separation, monitored assets, and clear layer boundaries.

skills.title: Client-server boundaries
skills.definition: A client requests a capability; a server validates the request, performs controlled work, and returns a documented response.

skills.title: HTTP methods and resource intent
skills.definition: Methods communicate intent: retrieval, creation, replacement, partial change, and deletion have different safety and idempotency properties.

skills.title: URLs, headers, bodies, and status codes
skills.definition: An HTTP message combines routing data, metadata, optional content, and a status that summarizes the outcome.

skills.title: Node.js modules and runtime state
skills.definition: A Node process loads modules into a dependency graph and keeps process-wide state separate from request-specific values.

skills.title: Event loop and asynchronous I/O
skills.definition: The event loop schedules callbacks after I/O completes; CPU-heavy work blocks progress while pending I/O does not.

skills.title: Configuration, files, and environment values
skills.definition: Configuration varies by environment and belongs outside source code; paths and failures must be handled explicitly.

skills.title: Building a minimal request pipeline
skills.definition: A server pipeline parses a request, routes it, performs domain work, and serializes one response exactly once.

skills.title: Errors, logging, and graceful shutdown
skills.definition: Operational errors need structured context, safe client messages, and orderly resource cleanup during shutdown.

skills.title: Express applications and routers
skills.definition: Routers partition the URL-method space into cohesive resource contracts instead of one growing conditional chain.

skills.title: Path parameters, queries, and bodies
skills.definition: Use path values for identity, query values for optional views, and bodies for structured commands or resource data.

skills.title: Middleware as ordered transformations
skills.definition: Middleware is an ordered pipeline; each stage either terminates the response or passes a well-defined request state forward.

skills.title: Validation and normalization
skills.definition: Validate shape and constraints at the boundary, then normalize accepted data into one internal representation.

skills.title: Central error handling
skills.definition: Domain, validation, and infrastructure failures map to stable error responses without exposing internal secrets.

skills.title: REST resource modeling
skills.definition: Resources use stable nouns, consistent representations, and predictable method semantics across collections and members.

skills.title: CORS, security headers, and rate decisions
skills.definition: Browser trust rules, protective headers, and fair-use limits reduce risk when configured for explicit origins and operations.

skills.title: Route tests and contract verification
skills.definition: Route tests control dependencies and assert status, headers, response shape, and side effects at meaningful boundaries.

skills.title: Relations, rows, columns, and keys
skills.definition: A relational table represents a set of similarly shaped facts; keys identify rows and connect related sets.

skills.title: Entities, cardinality, and ER models
skills.definition: Cardinality states how many records may relate, determining whether a foreign key or junction table represents the relationship.

skills.title: Selecting, filtering, and ordering
skills.definition: A query transforms a relation by choosing columns, retaining rows that satisfy predicates, and applying order only when requested.

skills.title: Joins and set relationships
skills.definition: A join pairs rows according to a predicate; join type determines which unmatched rows remain in the result.

skills.title: Aggregation and grouping
skills.definition: Grouping partitions rows by keys, then aggregate functions reduce each group to summary values.

skills.title: Writes, constraints, and transactions
skills.definition: A transaction moves the database from one valid state to another atomically while constraints guard invariants.

skills.title: Indexes and query plans
skills.definition: An index trades write cost and storage for faster ordered lookup; the query plan reveals whether that trade is being used.

skills.title: Normalization and schema migrations
skills.definition: Normalization reduces contradictory facts, while versioned migrations change schema and data in controlled, reversible steps.

skills.title: Password storage and verification
skills.definition: Store salted slow password hashes, compare them safely, and never retain or log the original secret.

skills.title: Sessions, tokens, and expiration
skills.definition: A credential binds an authenticated identity to a limited lifetime and scope; revocation and storage choices change the risk.

skills.title: Authentication versus authorization
skills.definition: Authentication establishes who is acting; authorization evaluates whether that actor may perform this action on this resource.

skills.title: Cookies, CSRF, and browser sessions
skills.definition: Secure cookie attributes protect transport and script access, while CSRF defenses ensure a state-changing request reflects user intent.

skills.title: Injection prevention and boundary validation
skills.definition: Treat external data as data, not executable syntax; parameterization and allowlisted validation preserve that boundary.

skills.title: Secrets and environment isolation
skills.definition: Secrets need restricted storage, rotation, least privilege, and separation from source, logs, and client-visible bundles.

skills.title: Audit events and privacy-aware logging
skills.definition: Audit logs record security-relevant who-what-when outcomes while minimizing sensitive content and protecting integrity.

skills.title: Threat modeling and layered controls
skills.definition: Map assets, entry points, trust boundaries, threats, and mitigations so multiple controls reduce both likelihood and impact.

skills.title: Versioning, pagination, and compatibility
skills.definition: Evolve contracts deliberately; pagination bounds work, and compatibility rules prevent existing clients from breaking unexpectedly.

skills.title: Testing pyramid and controlled dependencies
skills.definition: Use many fast unit tests, focused integration tests, and a small number of end-to-end tests around the highest-risk journeys.

skills.title: Observability with logs, metrics, and traces
skills.definition: Logs explain events, metrics reveal aggregate behavior, and traces connect work across a distributed request path.

skills.title: Caching and invalidation
skills.definition: A cache is a derived copy with a freshness policy; keys, lifetime, invalidation, and failure behavior determine correctness.

skills.title: Queues and background jobs
skills.definition: A queue separates arrival from processing; acknowledgments, retries, dead-letter handling, and idempotency prevent silent loss or duplicate harm.

skills.title: Concurrency and idempotent operations
skills.definition: Concurrent requests can interleave; atomic constraints and idempotency keys protect shared-state invariants.

skills.title: Containers, deployment, and health checks
skills.definition: A deployable service has reproducible artifacts, explicit configuration, health signals, migrations, and safe rollout/rollback steps.

skills.title: Scaling, reliability, and capacity
skills.definition: Capacity planning connects arrival rate, service time, utilization, latency, redundancy, and recovery objectives.

skills.title: Dart values, types, and null safety
skills.definition: Types describe valid operations, while nullable and non-nullable references make absence an explicit part of the contract.

skills.title: Variables, expressions, and functions
skills.definition: Functions map typed parameters to results or documented effects, and local variables keep intermediate state bounded.

skills.title: Conditions, loops, and exhaustive cases
skills.definition: Control flow partitions states or repeats a transition; every branch and termination boundary must be accounted for.

skills.title: Lists, maps, and immutable transformations
skills.definition: Collections encode order or key lookup; creating transformed values makes state changes easier to trace.

skills.title: Futures, async, and event timelines
skills.definition: A Future represents one eventual result, and await orders dependent steps while the UI event loop remains responsive.

skills.title: Widgets as immutable descriptions
skills.definition: A widget is an immutable configuration that describes part of the interface; Flutter rebuilds descriptions when inputs change.

skills.title: Stateful lifecycle and rebuilds
skills.definition: State persists across rebuilds for the same element identity and must release subscriptions or controllers when disposed.

skills.title: Packages, project structure, and debugging
skills.definition: A Flutter project separates source, assets, dependencies, and tests; analyzer and inspector evidence guide debugging.

skills.title: Flutter's constraints layout rule
skills.definition: Parents pass constraints down, children choose a permitted size, and parents position the resulting boxes.

skills.title: Row, Column, Flex, and available space
skills.definition: Flex layouts divide finite main-axis space by fixed needs and flex factors while cross-axis alignment controls placement.

skills.title: Scrolling lists and bounded viewports
skills.definition: A scrolling viewport needs bounded constraints and should lazily build large sequences to control memory and work.

skills.title: Navigation routes as a graph
skills.definition: Screens are nodes and allowed transitions are directed edges carrying typed arguments and returning optional results.

skills.title: Forms, controllers, and validation
skills.definition: A form collects named values, applies local and cross-field constraints, and submits only a valid snapshot.

skills.title: Themes and responsive composition
skills.definition: Themes encode shared design tokens, while responsive composition selects structures that satisfy current width and content constraints.

skills.title: Gestures, hit targets, and feedback
skills.definition: Gesture handling maps pointer sequences to semantic actions and must provide discoverable, immediate state feedback.

skills.title: Accessible widget semantics
skills.definition: Labels, roles, values, focus order, scalable text, and sufficient targets preserve meaning across assistive input modes.

skills.title: Local, shared, and derived state
skills.definition: Place mutable state at the narrowest owner that serves all consumers and compute derived values instead of storing duplicates.

skills.title: Explicit state transitions
skills.definition: Represent each user or system event as an action that transforms a known previous state into one next state.

skills.title: Notifiers and observable dependencies
skills.definition: Observers rebuild only when the values they depend on change; clear subscription ownership prevents leaks and stale views.

skills.title: Unidirectional data flow
skills.definition: State flows down to views and events flow back to an owner, creating a cycle with one authoritative source of truth.

skills.title: Repositories and service boundaries
skills.definition: A repository exposes domain-focused data operations while hiding whether data came from network, database, or cache.

skills.title: Dependency injection and test seams
skills.definition: Dependencies enter through constructors or providers so production implementations can be replaced by controlled test doubles.

skills.title: Loading, data, empty, and error states
skills.definition: Asynchronous screens need an explicit finite state model so no result or failure becomes an accidental null case.

skills.title: Layered feature architecture
skills.definition: Presentation, domain, and data layers point through narrow contracts, limiting the effect of change and simplifying tests.

skills.title: HTTP clients and typed serialization
skills.definition: Transport responses become trusted domain values only after status checks, decoding, and field validation.

skills.title: Cancellation, timeouts, and stale results
skills.definition: Asynchronous work needs lifetime rules so obsolete responses cannot overwrite newer screen state.

skills.title: Key-value storage and data sensitivity
skills.definition: Use key-value storage for small preferences, not relational data or secrets that require stronger protection.

skills.title: Local databases and schema evolution
skills.definition: Local tables preserve structured offline state; versioned migrations keep existing installations readable after schema change.

skills.title: Cache-aside and freshness decisions
skills.definition: Read from a cache under an explicit freshness policy, refresh from the source, and define behavior when either side fails.

skills.title: Offline queues and conflict resolution
skills.definition: Queued mutations need stable identities, retry policies, and a deterministic rule for resolving concurrent edits.

skills.title: Authentication and secure device storage
skills.definition: Tokens require protected storage, limited lifetime, redaction, and a clear logout or revocation path.

skills.title: Resilient offline-first data flow
skills.definition: An offline-first feature exposes local state immediately, synchronizes in the background, and communicates pending or conflicted changes.

skills.title: Unit, widget, and integration tests
skills.definition: Choose the smallest test boundary that proves the behavior: pure logic, rendered interaction, or multi-screen integration.

skills.title: Rebuild measurement and render performance
skills.definition: Profile frame timing and rebuild scope before changing code; stable inputs and smaller observers reduce unnecessary work.

skills.title: Memory, images, and resource lifetime
skills.definition: Large assets, caches, controllers, and subscriptions consume bounded resources that need sizing and disposal policies.

skills.title: Accessibility audits and inclusive flows
skills.definition: Verify semantics, focus, text scale, contrast, orientation, and error recovery across complete user journeys.

skills.title: Internationalization and locale-sensitive data
skills.definition: Translate messages and format dates, numbers, direction, and plural forms according to locale rather than concatenating fragments.

skills.title: Platform permissions and store readiness
skills.definition: Request the minimum permission at the moment of need and align declared capabilities, privacy notices, and behavior.

skills.title: Analytics, privacy, and failure monitoring
skills.definition: Collect only purposeful events, gain appropriate consent, avoid sensitive fields, and connect failures to actionable context.

skills.title: Continuous delivery and staged release
skills.definition: Automated checks produce signed builds, while staged rollout, monitoring, and rollback control release risk.

skills.title: JavaScript values and mobile input
skills.definition: External text and device values require explicit type, absence, and range checks before application logic uses them.

skills.title: Functions, arrays, and immutable updates
skills.definition: Pure functions and non-mutating collection operations make state transitions predictable and testable.

skills.title: Components and native render trees
skills.definition: A React Native component maps props and state to native-view descriptions organized as a tree.

skills.title: Props and one-way information flow
skills.definition: Parents pass read-only inputs downward; children communicate events upward through explicit callback contracts.

skills.title: State and event transitions
skills.definition: State records information that affects rendering, and events produce discrete transitions from one valid snapshot to another.

skills.title: Core components and platform differences
skills.definition: Use portable primitives by default and isolate platform-specific behavior behind narrow, tested boundaries.

skills.title: Styles, flex layout, and density
skills.definition: Mobile layout uses flex constraints and logical units so content adapts to screen size, density, and text scale.

skills.title: Project structure and debugging evidence
skills.definition: Separate features, shared components, and services; use logs, inspector state, and minimal reproduction to locate failures.

skills.title: Component composition and reusable contracts
skills.definition: Reusable components expose meaningful inputs and events while hiding visual and behavioral implementation details.

skills.title: Stack, tab, and modal navigation graphs
skills.definition: Navigation containers encode different graph relationships; a route should have one clear purpose and typed parameters.

skills.title: FlatList virtualization and stable keys
skills.definition: Virtualized lists render a moving window of items, and stable unique keys preserve item identity across updates.

skills.title: Controlled inputs and form state
skills.definition: Controlled fields derive displayed values from state and emit changes through a single validation-aware transition path.

skills.title: Validation and error recovery
skills.definition: Validation maps field and cross-field constraints to specific, accessible messages without destroying the learner's entered data.

skills.title: Responsive styling and safe areas
skills.definition: Layouts honor available dimensions, text scale, orientation, and system insets rather than assuming fixed coordinates.

skills.title: Touch interactions and feedback states
skills.definition: Press, long-press, swipe, disabled, loading, and success states need distinct rules and immediate perceptible feedback.

skills.title: Accessible navigation and forms
skills.definition: Screen titles, focus movement, labels, hints, errors, and touch targets preserve the task for assistive technologies.

skills.title: Local state, context, and ownership
skills.definition: Keep state local until multiple distant consumers need one authority; context distributes values but does not replace a state model.

skills.title: Reducers and finite UI states
skills.definition: A reducer maps state plus action to next state, while finite states prevent impossible loading-data-error combinations.

skills.title: Effects, cleanup, and dependency reasoning
skills.definition: Effects synchronize with external systems and must cancel subscriptions or ignore obsolete results when dependencies change.

skills.title: HTTP requests and response validation
skills.definition: A successful transport status is only one condition; decode and validate response structure before updating trusted state.

skills.title: Caching, retries, and server state
skills.definition: Server-state tools coordinate freshness, deduplication, retries, and invalidation without turning remote data into uncontrolled local copies.

skills.title: Service and repository boundaries
skills.definition: Network and storage details sit behind domain-oriented contracts that views can test without real infrastructure.

skills.title: Authentication state and protected routes
skills.definition: Authentication is an explicit state machine; route access reacts to verified identity without briefly exposing protected content.

skills.title: Feature-based application architecture
skills.definition: Group code by user capability and enforce dependency direction among presentation, domain, and infrastructure concerns.

skills.title: Permission flows and least access
skills.definition: Explain the user benefit, request only the needed device capability, and provide a usable denied-permission path.

skills.title: Camera, media, and resource cleanup
skills.definition: Device sessions have acquisition, active, paused, and released states; cleanup prevents privacy, battery, and memory problems.

skills.title: Local persistence and schema versions
skills.definition: Choose preference or database storage by data shape and evolve persistent records through tested version migrations.

skills.title: Secure storage and secret lifetimes
skills.definition: Sensitive tokens belong in platform-protected storage, with short lifetime, redacted diagnostics, and explicit revocation.

skills.title: Connectivity state and offline feedback
skills.definition: Connectivity is evidence, not proof of service availability; show cached, pending, failed, and synchronized states explicitly.

skills.title: Mutation queues and conflict policies
skills.definition: Offline writes need unique operation IDs, ordering rules, bounded retries, and deterministic merge or user-resolution behavior.

skills.title: Deep links and untrusted external input
skills.definition: Treat every deep-link parameter as untrusted, validate destination and identity state, and reject unsupported transitions.

skills.title: Threat modeling a mobile feature
skills.definition: Map local assets, device boundaries, network boundaries, entry points, abuse cases, and layered mitigations before implementation.

skills.title: Unit, component, and device tests
skills.definition: Match test scope to risk and control time, network, storage, and navigation dependencies for reproducible evidence.

skills.title: Render profiling and memoization
skills.definition: Measure component commits and frame delays; memoization helps only when comparison cost is lower than avoided work.

skills.title: Lists, images, and startup performance
skills.definition: Windowing, correctly sized assets, deferred work, and bundle analysis target the largest measured delays.

skills.title: Native bridges and failure boundaries
skills.definition: Crossing the JavaScript-native boundary has serialization and lifetime costs that need narrow interfaces and error handling.

skills.title: Accessibility and international release
skills.definition: Test screen-reader flow, focus, scaling, contrast, right-to-left layout, and locale formatting on real journeys.

skills.title: Privacy declarations and store policies
skills.definition: Declared data use, permissions, SDK behavior, and in-app consent must describe the same actual system.

skills.title: Crash monitoring and release health
skills.definition: Symbolicated crashes, non-sensitive context, version cohorts, and service indicators reveal whether a release is safe.

skills.title: Automated builds and phased rollout
skills.definition: Repeatable signed builds plus staged exposure, monitoring thresholds, and rollback reduce the impact of release defects.

skills.title: Assets, value, and security objectives
skills.definition: Security begins by identifying what has value, who depends on it, and which confidentiality, integrity, and availability properties matter.

skills.title: Threats, vulnerabilities, and controls
skills.definition: A threat can exploit a vulnerability; a control prevents, detects, or helps recover from the resulting harm.

skills.title: Likelihood, impact, and risk
skills.definition: Risk priority combines evidence about likelihood and impact instead of treating every weakness as equally urgent.

skills.title: Confidentiality decisions
skills.definition: Confidentiality limits information disclosure through classification, least privilege, secure transport, and controlled sharing.

skills.title: Integrity decisions
skills.definition: Integrity protects authorized and accurate change through validation, permissions, hashes, versioning, and audit evidence.

skills.title: Availability and resilience
skills.definition: Availability uses redundancy, capacity, backups, monitoring, and recovery plans to keep required services usable.

skills.title: Trust boundaries and attack surfaces
skills.definition: A trust boundary marks where assumptions change; every exposed input or capability expands the attack surface that controls must cover.

skills.title: Security trade-offs and defense in depth
skills.definition: Layered controls reduce single points of failure while decisions balance risk reduction, usability, cost, and operational burden.

skills.title: Accounts, processes, and least privilege
skills.definition: Separate identities and grant each process only the resources required for its documented task.

skills.title: Permissions and secure configuration
skills.definition: Ownership and access rules should start restrictive, be reviewed against need, and avoid unsafe convenience defaults.

skills.title: Patch and vulnerability management
skills.definition: Inventory systems, assess exposure and impact, test updates, deploy by priority, and verify remediation.

skills.title: Network layers and packet journeys
skills.definition: Data is encapsulated across layers and forwarded hop by hop; each boundary exposes different metadata and control points.

skills.title: Addressing, ports, and service exposure
skills.definition: An address locates a host and a port identifies a service endpoint; exposed listeners must match documented need.

skills.title: DNS, TLS, and secure protocol properties
skills.definition: DNS maps names, while TLS authenticates endpoints and protects transport confidentiality and integrity when validation succeeds.

skills.title: Segmentation and firewall decisions
skills.definition: Segmentation limits paths between trust zones; firewall rules should allow explicit required flows and deny unnecessary reachability.

skills.title: Defensive network log analysis
skills.definition: Correlate timestamps, sources, destinations, actions, and baselines to distinguish expected operations from events requiring investigation.

skills.title: Application trust boundaries
skills.definition: Map browser, API, database, third-party, and administrator boundaries so every untrusted transition has validation and authorization.

skills.title: Input validation and output encoding
skills.definition: Validate input for expected shape and encode output for its destination context; the two controls solve different boundary problems.

skills.title: Authentication and session defense
skills.definition: Strong identity proof, protected credentials, expiration, revocation, and anomaly detection reduce account and session risk.

skills.title: Authorization and object-level access
skills.definition: Every protected operation re-evaluates the actor, action, and target object on the server, regardless of interface visibility.

skills.title: Secure API contracts and rate controls
skills.definition: Strict schemas, bounded payloads, consistent errors, quotas, and monitoring limit misuse and accidental overload.

skills.title: Browser-origin protections
skills.definition: Origin policy, safe cookie attributes, CSRF defenses, and content restrictions reduce unintended cross-site actions and script execution.

skills.title: Dependency and software-supply-chain risk
skills.definition: Pin, verify, inventory, scan, minimize, and update dependencies through reviewed and reproducible build steps.

skills.title: Threat modeling and remediation planning
skills.definition: Prioritize feasible abuse paths, select layered controls, assign owners and deadlines, then verify risk reduction.

skills.title: Cryptographic goals and threat models
skills.definition: Choose cryptography only after defining the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, or non-repudiation property and the adversary's capability.

skills.title: Hash functions and integrity evidence
skills.definition: A cryptographic hash maps arbitrary input to a fixed digest with collision and preimage resistance; it does not hide data.

skills.title: Symmetric encryption and nonce rules
skills.definition: Symmetric encryption uses one shared secret, and modern authenticated modes require unique nonces under a key.

skills.title: Public-key encryption and signatures
skills.definition: Public-key systems separate public and private operations; encryption protects secrecy while signatures provide origin and integrity evidence.

skills.title: Certificates and trust chains
skills.definition: A certificate binds an identity to a public key, and validation checks chain, hostname, time, purpose, and revocation evidence.

skills.title: Identity lifecycle and multi-factor controls
skills.definition: Provisioning, authentication, recovery, role change, and deprovisioning form one identity lifecycle with high-risk transitions.

skills.title: Data classification and retention
skills.definition: Classification determines handling, access, encryption, sharing, retention, and verified deletion requirements.

skills.title: Key management and cryptographic agility
skills.definition: Keys need generation, storage, access control, rotation, backup, revocation, and replacement plans independent of application code.

skills.title: Security telemetry and log quality
skills.definition: Useful telemetry has synchronized time, stable identity, event outcome, source context, protected integrity, and bounded sensitive data.

skills.title: Baselines, detections, and false positives
skills.definition: A detection compares observable behavior to a rule or baseline; thresholds balance missed events against investigation cost.

skills.title: Triage and evidence preservation
skills.definition: Triage establishes scope and urgency while recording provenance and preserving original evidence before deeper analysis.

skills.title: Incident-response lifecycle
skills.definition: Preparation, identification, containment, eradication, recovery, and learning form an iterative response process.

skills.title: Containment and business trade-offs
skills.definition: Containment limits ongoing harm but must consider evidence, safety, service dependency, and the possibility of alerting an adversary.

skills.title: Recovery and validation
skills.definition: Recovery restores trusted service in stages and verifies configuration, data integrity, monitoring, and recurrence controls.

skills.title: Communication and decision records
skills.definition: Roles, severity, audience, cadence, known facts, uncertainty, and decisions keep technical and organizational response aligned.

skills.title: Post-incident learning and control improvement
skills.definition: A blameless review connects contributing conditions to owned corrective actions and measurable verification.

skills.title: Written authorization and legal boundaries
skills.definition: Testing begins only after a named owner grants written permission for specific systems, dates, methods, and personnel.

skills.title: Rules of engagement
skills.definition: Rules define communication, permitted techniques, stop conditions, data handling, evidence retention, and escalation contacts.

skills.title: Scope as explicit sets
skills.definition: In-scope targets and actions are allowlisted sets; ambiguity, third-party ownership, or missing entries mean stop and clarify.

skills.title: Isolated lab architecture
skills.definition: A safe practice lab uses fictional data, isolated networking, disposable machines, snapshots, and no route to public targets.

skills.title: Safety stop conditions
skills.definition: Unexpected impact, sensitive data, unstable service, scope uncertainty, or lost monitoring triggers an immediate pause and notification.

skills.title: Evidence handling and privacy
skills.definition: Collect the minimum proof, timestamp it, protect integrity, restrict access, and remove it according to the agreed retention rule.

skills.title: Risk communication without exaggeration
skills.definition: Describe observable evidence, realistic preconditions, potential impact, uncertainty, and remediation without claiming unverified compromise.

skills.title: Professional conduct and handoff
skills.definition: Respect scope, minimize disruption, communicate promptly, and transfer findings through approved channels with clear ownership.

skills.title: Authorized asset inventory
skills.definition: Start from owner-provided inventory and record hostname, service, owner, purpose, environment, and scope status for fictional lab assets.

skills.title: Passive versus active evidence
skills.definition: Passive review uses supplied records, while active checks send traffic; the authorization and impact profile differs.

skills.title: Service exposure mapping
skills.definition: Map only approved lab addresses to documented services and compare observed exposure with the intended architecture.

skills.title: Metadata and information leakage
skills.definition: Public or supplied metadata can reveal versions, paths, contacts, or structure; report only evidence within scope and minimize collected personal data.

skills.title: Trust-boundary diagrams
skills.definition: Place assets into zones and draw permitted data flows so unexpected pathways become review questions rather than exploitation attempts.

skills.title: Evidence confidence and corroboration
skills.definition: One signal may be stale or ambiguous; confidence increases when independent approved sources agree.

skills.title: Exposure prioritization
skills.definition: Prioritize externally reachable, sensitive, high-impact, weakly controlled, and owner-unknown assets for defensive review.

skills.title: Reconnaissance reporting and remediation
skills.definition: Turn inventory gaps and unintended exposure into asset ownership, closure, segmentation, and monitoring actions.

skills.title: Finding versus verified vulnerability
skills.definition: A tool finding is a hypothesis; safe validation confirms affected asset, condition, version, configuration, and evidence without harmful exploitation.

skills.title: Scanner scope and safe configuration
skills.definition: Limit a lab assessment by allowlisted targets, low-impact checks, rate, timing, credentials, exclusions, and stop monitoring.

skills.title: False positives and false negatives
skills.definition: Corroborate results because imperfect detection can report absent weaknesses or miss present ones.

skills.title: Version and configuration evidence
skills.definition: Compare observed approved-lab facts with vendor or policy criteria while accounting for backports and compensating controls.

skills.title: Risk rating with context
skills.definition: Severity combines technical impact, exploit preconditions, exposure, asset value, existing controls, and confidence.

skills.title: Minimal proof and non-destructive validation
skills.definition: Collect the least evidence that demonstrates the condition; do not extract real data, alter state, bypass controls, or establish persistence.

skills.title: Remediation selection and verification
skills.definition: Prefer root-cause fixes, define compensating controls when needed, retest the exact condition, and document residual risk.

skills.title: Assessment quality and reproducibility
skills.definition: A finding records scope, time, environment, method class, evidence, assumptions, impact, fix, and safe retest steps.

skills.title: Safe web-lab request mapping
skills.definition: Within the isolated lab, map documented routes, methods, parameters, identity states, and expected responses without probing outside scope.

skills.title: Validation review with inert test data
skills.definition: Use harmless boundary strings and schema cases to verify that the fictional lab accepts only intended shapes and lengths.

skills.title: Authorization matrix review
skills.definition: Build an actor-action-resource matrix and verify allowed and denied outcomes using only provided fictional accounts.

skills.title: Session configuration review
skills.definition: Inspect lab cookie flags, expiration, rotation, logout, and error behavior without attempting credential theft or session hijacking.

skills.title: Browser security-header review
skills.definition: Compare supplied lab headers with the application's resource needs and recommend restrictive, testable policies.

skills.title: API error and rate-control review
skills.definition: Verify that fictional endpoints return consistent non-sensitive errors and bounded responses under approved low-rate tests.

skills.title: Dependency and deployment review
skills.definition: Assess supplied manifests, lockfiles, build settings, and fictional advisories without executing untrusted packages.

skills.title: Web finding remediation and retest
skills.definition: Connect each safe lab observation to root cause, code or configuration control, regression test, and residual-risk statement.

skills.title: Executive and technical audiences
skills.definition: Executives need risk and decisions; technical owners need reproducible evidence, root cause, exact affected scope, and verification criteria.

skills.title: Finding anatomy and evidence quality
skills.definition: A complete finding separates observation, preconditions, impact, likelihood, evidence, affected assets, remediation, and confidence.

skills.title: Consistent risk rating
skills.definition: Use a documented rubric and business context so similar evidence receives comparable priority and uncertainty remains visible.

skills.title: Root cause and remediation options
skills.definition: Distinguish immediate containment, durable correction, compensating control, owner, dependency, cost, and target date.

skills.title: Retesting and closure criteria
skills.definition: Close a finding only when the agreed control is deployed, the original condition no longer holds, regression evidence passes, and residual risk is accepted.

skills.title: Metrics without misleading incentives
skills.definition: Track exposure age, verified closure, recurrence, and coverage rather than rewarding raw finding counts.

skills.title: Responsible disclosure and communication
skills.definition: Use authorized channels, protect details, allow coordinated remediation time, and follow legal and organizational requirements.

skills.title: End-to-end assessment portfolio
skills.definition: A professional portfolio links authorization, scope, methods, evidence, prioritized findings, remediation, retest, and lessons learned.

skills.title: Array indices and contiguous sequence models
skills.definition: An array maps integer positions to ordered values; valid indices form the half-open range from zero to length.

skills.title: Traversal and loop invariants
skills.definition: During left-to-right traversal, define what has been proven about the processed prefix before advancing the boundary.

skills.title: Insertion, deletion, and shifting cost
skills.definition: Changing an array's middle may shift a suffix, so cost grows with the number of displaced elements.

skills.title: Strings as sequences
skills.definition: String algorithms reason about characters or code points, order, boundaries, and often immutable transformations.

skills.title: Frequency counting with bounded symbols
skills.definition: A frequency table maps each allowed symbol to its occurrence count and preserves the invariant that counts sum to processed items.

skills.title: Two-dimensional arrays and coordinates
skills.definition: A grid maps row-column pairs to values; neighbor rules and boundary checks define valid movement.

skills.title: Prefix summaries
skills.definition: A prefix array stores cumulative information so a range query becomes the difference between two boundary summaries.

skills.title: Choosing array and string representations
skills.definition: Choose a representation whose order, access, mutation, memory, and character-handling properties match the operations.

skills.title: Nodes, links, and list invariants
skills.definition: A linked list is a chain of nodes; each next reference preserves reachability and the tail terminates with no successor.

skills.title: Linked-list traversal and search
skills.definition: Traversal follows links rather than numeric indices and must stop at the end or when the target is found.

skills.title: Insertion and deletion by rewiring
skills.definition: Local list changes update a small set of links, but only after preserving references to the remaining chain.

skills.title: Fast and slow pointer reasoning
skills.definition: Pointers moving at different rates reveal middle positions or cycles through relative-distance invariants.

skills.title: Stacks and last-in-first-out
skills.definition: A stack exposes only the most recently added unremoved item, supporting nested and reversal processes.

skills.title: Queues and first-in-first-out
skills.definition: A queue removes items in arrival order and needs separate front and rear state for efficient operations.

skills.title: Deques and monotonic queues
skills.definition: A deque supports both ends; a monotonic deque discards dominated candidates while preserving useful order.

skills.title: Selecting linear structures
skills.definition: Choose arrays, lists, stacks, queues, or deques from required access position, update pattern, order, and complexity.

skills.title: Key-value and membership models
skills.definition: A map associates unique keys with values, while a set records only whether a key is present.

skills.title: Hash functions and bucket placement
skills.definition: A hash function deterministically maps a key to a numeric code used to select a bounded bucket.

skills.title: Collisions and equality
skills.definition: Different keys can share a bucket, so collision handling must still use correct key equality to distinguish them.

skills.title: Load factor and resizing
skills.definition: As entries per bucket rise, expected operation cost worsens; resizing expands capacity and redistributes entries.

skills.title: Frequency maps and counting invariants
skills.definition: After processing a prefix, each stored value equals the exact number of times its key appeared in that prefix.

skills.title: Grouping and indexing by derived keys
skills.definition: A derived canonical key can group records that share a property, such as normalized letters or category.

skills.title: Memoization and cached subproblems
skills.definition: Memoization maps a complete subproblem state to its solved result, avoiding repeated work without changing correctness.

skills.title: Hash-structure trade-offs
skills.definition: Expected constant-time lookup depends on good hashing, while ordering, worst-case needs, memory, and key mutability may favor another structure.

skills.title: Tree vocabulary and recursive structure
skills.definition: A tree has one root and unique parent paths; every subtree is itself a tree with smaller scope.

skills.title: Depth-first and breadth-first traversal
skills.definition: Depth-first traversal follows a branch before siblings, while breadth-first traversal processes nodes by distance from the root.

skills.title: Binary search tree invariant
skills.definition: Every node partitions keys so left-subtree values precede it and right-subtree values follow it under the chosen ordering rule.

skills.title: BST search, insertion, and deletion
skills.definition: Operations follow the ordering invariant; deletion reconnects subtrees while preserving every remaining key's order.

skills.title: Balanced height and logarithmic paths
skills.definition: Keeping subtree heights controlled prevents an ordered tree from degenerating into a linear chain.

skills.title: Heap order and complete shape
skills.definition: A binary heap combines complete-tree shape with parent priority, guaranteeing fast access to one extreme rather than full order.

skills.title: Priority queues and top-k reasoning
skills.definition: A priority queue repeatedly exposes the highest- or lowest-priority item; a bounded heap can retain the best k candidates.

skills.title: Choosing hierarchical structures
skills.definition: Select a tree, BST, heap, or flat structure according to hierarchy, ordered lookup, priority access, update cost, and memory.

skills.title: Graph vertices, edges, and representations
skills.definition: A graph models entities and relationships; adjacency lists favor sparse edges while matrices favor constant-time edge checks.

skills.title: Graph traversal and visited invariants
skills.definition: BFS or DFS expands reachable vertices while a visited set ensures each vertex is finalized according to the traversal rule.

skills.title: Shortest paths in unweighted graphs
skills.definition: BFS discovers vertices in nondecreasing edge distance, so the first discovery gives a shortest unweighted path.

skills.title: Directed acyclic graphs and topological order
skills.definition: A topological order places every directed prerequisite before its dependent and exists only when there is no directed cycle.

skills.title: Weighted paths and relaxation
skills.definition: Relaxation improves a best-known distance when an edge offers a cheaper route; algorithm choice depends on weight properties.

skills.title: Disjoint sets and connectivity
skills.definition: Union-find maintains partitions under union and connectivity queries using representative parents, path compression, and rank or size.

skills.title: Tries and prefix structure
skills.definition: A trie shares prefixes along root-to-node paths, trading memory for operations proportional to key length.

skills.title: Advanced structure selection
skills.definition: Choose representations by operation mix, density, ordering, connectivity, prefix needs, guarantees, and implementation cost.

skills.title: Input size and operation counting
skills.definition: Define input size, identify the repeated primitive operation, and express how its count grows as input scales.

skills.title: Time and space complexity classes
skills.definition: Asymptotic bounds compare growth while ignoring constant factors, but auxiliary memory and real constraints still affect choice.

skills.title: Linear search and early termination
skills.definition: Linear search preserves that the target is absent from the processed prefix and stops on discovery or exhaustion.

skills.title: Binary search and boundary invariants
skills.definition: Binary search maintains a sorted candidate interval containing every possible answer and removes a proven half each step.

skills.title: Stable comparison sorting
skills.definition: A stable sort preserves the input order of equal keys, which matters when records have earlier ordering decisions.

skills.title: Divide-and-conquer sorting
skills.definition: Merge sort divides, solves smaller arrays, and merges sorted sequences; quicksort partitions around a pivot with data-dependent balance.

skills.title: Non-comparison sorting constraints
skills.definition: Counting or bucket methods exploit bounded key structure to avoid comparison lower bounds at a memory cost.

skills.title: Selecting and explaining an algorithm
skills.definition: Choose from input properties, operation costs, memory, stability, worst-case guarantees, and implementation risk, then justify the trade-off.

skills.title: Opposite-direction two pointers
skills.definition: On ordered data, pointer movement discards a region proven unable to contain a solution.

skills.title: Same-direction read and write pointers
skills.definition: A read pointer inspects each item while a write pointer marks the boundary of the valid compacted prefix.

skills.title: Fixed-size sliding windows
skills.definition: Update a fixed window by adding the entering item and removing the leaving item instead of recomputing the aggregate.

skills.title: Variable windows with monotonic constraints
skills.definition: Expand to gain candidates and shrink while invalid, provided the constraint changes monotonically with window boundaries.

skills.title: Prefix sums and range queries
skills.definition: Cumulative boundaries convert an interval sum into one subtraction after linear preprocessing.

skills.title: Prefix frequencies and balance states
skills.definition: Equal prefix states imply that the segment between them has zero net change under the tracked balance.

skills.title: Monotonic stacks and next-boundary problems
skills.definition: A monotonic stack keeps unresolved candidates in order and removes those resolved by the current value.

skills.title: Pattern selection and counterexamples
skills.definition: Pointer and window methods require order or monotonicity; construct counterexamples before applying them to arbitrary constraints.

skills.title: Recursive contracts and base cases
skills.definition: A recursive function solves one state by reducing it to smaller states and needs base cases that cover every terminating path.

skills.title: Call stacks and recurrence traces
skills.definition: Each call owns parameters and local state; the call tree reveals repeated work and maximum stack depth.

skills.title: Backtracking state and undo
skills.definition: Choose, explore, and undo so every branch starts from the same valid prefix state.

skills.title: Pruning invalid and dominated branches
skills.definition: Pruning is correct only when a predicate proves that no completion of the current partial state can improve or satisfy the answer.

skills.title: Permutations, combinations, and duplicates
skills.definition: State representation and start boundaries determine whether order matters and whether equal choices create duplicate solutions.

skills.title: Greedy choice properties
skills.definition: A greedy method is valid when a locally preferred choice can be exchanged into some optimal solution without reducing quality.

skills.title: Interval and scheduling decisions
skills.definition: Sorting by the right boundary can expose an exchange argument for maximizing compatible choices in specific interval problems.

skills.title: Proving or rejecting greedy solutions
skills.definition: Use exchange proofs, stays-ahead invariants, and small counterexamples rather than trusting locally attractive choices.

skills.title: Optimal substructure and overlapping states
skills.definition: Dynamic programming applies when optimal solutions combine optimal subproblem results and the same states recur.

skills.title: State definition and sufficient information
skills.definition: A DP state must contain exactly the information needed to evaluate future choices without remembering the entire history.

skills.title: Transitions and dependency graphs
skills.definition: A transition combines already solved predecessor states, forming an acyclic dependency graph or a controlled iterative process.

skills.title: Memoization and tabulation
skills.definition: Memoization explores needed states top-down; tabulation orders all relevant states bottom-up according to dependencies.

skills.title: One-dimensional sequence DP
skills.definition: Sequence states often represent the best answer for a prefix or endpoint, with transitions considering the final decision.

skills.title: Grid and path DP
skills.definition: Grid states aggregate valid predecessor paths or costs while boundaries encode unreachable or base positions.

skills.title: Knapsack-style choice DP
skills.definition: Choice states track an item boundary and limited resource; iteration direction determines whether an item may be reused.

skills.title: Space optimization and correctness proof
skills.definition: Discard old DP layers only after proving no future transition depends on them, and state the invariant for the compressed array.

skills.title: Clarifying ambiguous problem statements
skills.definition: Restate the input-output contract, constraints, examples, edge cases, and allowed assumptions before choosing a method.

skills.title: From brute force to bottleneck
skills.definition: Start with a correct baseline, locate the operation causing excessive growth, and replace it using structure or precomputation.

skills.title: Selecting mixed patterns
skills.definition: Classify order, locality, repetition, hierarchy, connectivity, and optimization structure before selecting a pattern.

skills.title: Correctness explanations with invariants
skills.definition: Explain initialization, preservation, termination, and why the invariant implies the required result.

skills.title: Complexity under realistic constraints
skills.definition: Relate time, space, recursion depth, numeric range, and input distribution to actual limits instead of naming Big-O alone.

skills.title: Testing strategy and adversarial cases
skills.definition: Cover empty, minimal, maximal, duplicate, ordered, disconnected, overflow, and constraint-boundary cases relevant to the contract.

skills.title: Communicating while coding
skills.definition: Narrate decisions, name invariants, check intermediate states, and respond to feedback without abandoning the proven contract.

skills.title: Debugging and post-solution refinement
skills.definition: Trace the first divergent state, repair the cause, rerun targeted tests, then discuss alternatives and trade-offs.

skills.title: Examples, features, labels, and matrices
skills.definition: Represent n examples with d numeric features as an n-by-d matrix and align each supervised target with exactly one row.

skills.title: Vectors, dot products, and similarity
skills.definition: A dot product combines aligned components into a weighted sum; magnitude and angle affect how it should be interpreted.

skills.title: Functions and model mappings
skills.definition: A model is a parameterized function that maps an input vector to a prediction with a documented output meaning.

skills.title: Summary statistics and distributions
skills.definition: Center, spread, quantiles, and shape describe different distribution properties and can reveal outliers or skew.

skills.title: Scaling and normalization
skills.definition: Rescaling changes feature geometry and optimization behavior; fit transformation parameters only on training data.

skills.title: Missing values and data validity
skills.definition: Absence can be informative or accidental; document its mechanism, choose a treatment, and preserve an indicator when needed.

skills.title: Dataset splits and leakage prevention
skills.definition: Training, validation, and test sets serve different decisions, and no future or target-derived information may cross backward.

skills.title: Reproducible data pipelines
skills.definition: Version data, code, parameters, random seeds, and environment so the same inputs produce traceable outputs.

skills.title: Regression as numeric prediction
skills.definition: Regression maps features to a continuous value and is evaluated against the size and meaning of numeric errors.

skills.title: Classification and decision boundaries
skills.definition: Classification estimates class evidence or probability and applies a threshold or decision rule tied to error costs.

skills.title: Linear models and weighted features
skills.definition: A linear model combines features through weights and an intercept, creating an interpretable flat decision surface.

skills.title: Tree-based partitioning
skills.definition: A decision tree recursively partitions feature space by rules that improve target separation while risking overfit when too deep.

skills.title: Nearest-neighbor reasoning
skills.definition: Nearest-neighbor methods predict from nearby training examples under a chosen distance and scaling, with storage and query costs.

skills.title: Clustering and unsupervised objectives
skills.definition: Clustering groups examples by an explicit similarity objective, but groups do not automatically equal meaningful real-world categories.

skills.title: Train, fit, predict, and transform
skills.definition: Fitting learns parameters from training data; prediction applies the learned mapping, while transformation changes representations.

skills.title: Model assumptions and baseline comparisons
skills.definition: A simple baseline exposes whether a model adds useful signal and which assumptions fail on important subgroups or ranges.

skills.title: Feature engineering and valid information
skills.definition: Create features from information available at prediction time and document their meaning, units, and failure cases.

skills.title: Confusion matrices
skills.definition: A confusion matrix counts actual-versus-predicted classes and is the source for precision, recall, specificity, and related metrics.

skills.title: Thresholds and asymmetric error costs
skills.definition: Changing a score threshold trades false positives against false negatives; choose it from operational costs and capacity.

skills.title: Regression metrics and scale
skills.definition: MAE, squared-error measures, and relative metrics weight errors differently and must be interpreted in target units and distribution.

skills.title: Cross-validation and model selection
skills.definition: Use validation folds to estimate choice performance while keeping the final test set untouched until decisions are complete.

skills.title: Underfitting, overfitting, and regularization
skills.definition: Compare training and validation behavior; regularization constrains flexibility to improve generalization rather than training fit.

skills.title: Bias, subgroup evaluation, and uncertainty
skills.definition: Aggregate performance can hide unequal errors; evaluate meaningful groups with sample sizes and uncertainty visible.

skills.title: Experiment tracking and honest conclusions
skills.definition: Record hypotheses, configurations, metrics, seeds, exclusions, and negative results before drawing bounded conclusions.

skills.title: Neurons, layers, and tensor shapes
skills.definition: A layer maps an input tensor shape to an output shape using learned parameters; shape compatibility is a structural invariant.

skills.title: Activations and nonlinear functions
skills.definition: Nonlinear activations allow stacked layers to represent more than one linear transformation, while saturation affects gradients.

skills.title: Loss functions and learning objectives
skills.definition: A loss converts prediction error into a scalar training signal and must match output meaning, data distribution, and error costs.

skills.title: Gradients and backpropagation
skills.definition: Backpropagation applies the chain rule through the computation graph to assign each parameter its contribution to loss change.

skills.title: Gradient descent and learning rates
skills.definition: An optimizer updates parameters opposite the estimated gradient; step size balances slow progress against instability.

skills.title: Batches, epochs, and stochastic estimates
skills.definition: A batch estimates the full-data gradient, an epoch processes the training set, and shuffling changes correlation in updates.

skills.title: Regularization and generalization
skills.definition: Weight penalties, data augmentation, dropout, and early stopping constrain effective capacity in different ways.

skills.title: Training diagnostics and failure modes
skills.definition: Learning curves, gradient norms, data checks, and baseline comparisons distinguish optimization, representation, leakage, and overfit problems.

skills.title: Training-serving consistency
skills.definition: Production preprocessing and feature definitions must match training exactly or predictions operate on a different input space.

skills.title: Model packaging and inference contracts
skills.definition: A deployable model specifies version, feature schema, output semantics, latency, resource limits, and failure behavior.

skills.title: Data drift and performance monitoring
skills.definition: Monitor input and prediction distributions continuously, but confirm quality drift with delayed ground truth when available.

skills.title: Feedback loops and delayed labels
skills.definition: Model decisions can change future data; evaluation must account for selection effects, missing outcomes, and label delay.

skills.title: Safe rollout and rollback
skills.definition: Shadow, canary, or staged deployment limits exposure while predefined metrics and rollback criteria control risk.

skills.title: Fairness, privacy, and human oversight
skills.definition: Evaluate affected groups, minimize data, protect sensitive attributes, define appeal, and assign humans meaningful decision authority.

skills.title: Model cards and decision documentation
skills.definition: Document purpose, data, metrics, limitations, ethical considerations, owners, and prohibited uses for accountable deployment.

skills.title: Incident response for ML systems
skills.definition: Detect harmful behavior, contain model or data changes, preserve evidence, restore a safe baseline, and update controls from lessons learned.

skills.title: Text units, Unicode, and normalization
skills.definition: Text is encoded as Unicode sequences; normalization choices can merge visually equivalent forms while case and punctuation may carry meaning.

skills.title: Tokenization and vocabulary boundaries
skills.definition: A tokenizer maps text to token IDs under a fixed vocabulary, and different segmentations change sequence length and information sharing.

skills.title: Bag-of-words vectors
skills.definition: A bag-of-words vector records token counts or presence while discarding order, producing a sparse document-feature matrix.

skills.title: TF-IDF weighting
skills.definition: TF-IDF raises terms frequent in one document but rare across the collection, with smoothing and normalization affecting scale.

skills.title: N-grams and local order
skills.definition: Word or character n-grams retain bounded local order at the cost of a much larger feature space.

skills.title: Text cleaning without destroying signal
skills.definition: Every cleaning step encodes an assumption; validate whether punctuation, casing, numbers, dialect, or spelling are useful for the task.

skills.title: Sequence padding, masks, and lengths
skills.definition: Batches align variable sequences using padding, while masks ensure padded positions do not affect computation or evaluation.

skills.title: Text data pipelines and leakage
skills.definition: Split by the real deployment unit before fitting vocabulary or statistics, and track source, consent, duplicates, and labels.

skills.title: Text classification contracts
skills.definition: Define allowed inputs, label meaning, multi-class or multi-label structure, uncertainty, and the operational action triggered by a prediction.

skills.title: Sparse linear text classifiers
skills.definition: Linear classifiers weight token features, creating a transparent baseline that often performs strongly on limited labeled data.

skills.title: Dense embeddings and vector geometry
skills.definition: An embedding maps an item to a dense vector where distance or angle is intended to reflect selected relationships.

skills.title: Cosine similarity
skills.definition: Cosine similarity compares vector direction rather than magnitude, but meaningful interpretation still depends on how the embeddings were trained.

skills.title: Nearest-neighbor semantic retrieval
skills.definition: Embed a query and candidates under the same model, retrieve nearby vectors, then validate relevance with task-specific labels.

skills.title: Class imbalance and threshold choice
skills.definition: Imbalanced labels require per-class metrics, suitable sampling or weighting, and thresholds tied to error costs.

skills.title: Embedding bias and representation limits
skills.definition: Vector neighborhoods can reproduce training associations and underrepresent languages, dialects, or domains.

skills.title: Evaluation sets and error analysis
skills.definition: Stratify errors by class, language form, length, ambiguity, and subgroup to turn metric gaps into model or data actions.

skills.title: Sequence state and recurrent models
skills.definition: A recurrent model updates a hidden state from the current token and previous state, compressing prefix information through time.

skills.title: Long-range dependencies and gradient paths
skills.definition: Long sequences create repeated transformations that can weaken or amplify gradients and overload a fixed hidden state.

skills.title: Attention as weighted aggregation
skills.definition: Attention computes query-key compatibility, normalizes weights, and returns a weighted sum of value vectors.

skills.title: Self-attention tensor shapes
skills.definition: Each sequence position produces queries, keys, and values; pairwise scores create a sequence-by-sequence relationship matrix.

skills.title: Position information
skills.definition: Because attention alone is insensitive to token order, positional features inject absolute or relative sequence relationships.

skills.title: Transformer blocks and residual paths
skills.definition: Attention and feed-forward transformations are wrapped with residual connections and normalization to preserve information and trainability.

skills.title: Causal and padding masks
skills.definition: A causal mask blocks future positions, while a padding mask blocks artificial batch padding; they encode different constraints.

skills.title: Pretraining, fine-tuning, and limitations
skills.definition: Pretraining learns broad statistical representations; adaptation changes task behavior but does not guarantee truth, fairness, or domain coverage.

skills.title: Prompt contracts and bounded tasks
skills.definition: A reliable prompt states role, input boundaries, required output schema, uncertainty behavior, and prohibited actions.

skills.title: Structured output and schema validation
skills.definition: Generated text becomes application data only after parsing, schema validation, and safe handling of missing or extra fields.

skills.title: Retrieval pipelines
skills.definition: A retrieval system chunks approved sources, indexes representations, retrieves candidates, and supplies traceable context for generation.

skills.title: Chunking, ranking, and context budgets
skills.definition: Chunk boundaries trade completeness against specificity, while reranking and token budgets determine which evidence reaches the model.

skills.title: Grounding and citation verification
skills.definition: A grounded answer must be supported by retrieved evidence, and citation checks must verify that the cited passage entails the claim.

skills.title: Tool use and permission boundaries
skills.definition: Treat model-proposed actions as untrusted plans; validate arguments, permissions, target identity, side effects, and confirmation needs.

skills.title: Conversation state and memory
skills.definition: Store only purposeful, consented facts with provenance, lifetime, user controls, and separation between instructions and retrieved content.

skills.title: Failure modes and resilient application design
skills.definition: Handle hallucination, prompt injection, missing evidence, latency, refusal, tool error, and partial output as explicit states.

skills.title: Task-specific evaluation design
skills.definition: Define representative inputs, reference criteria, scoring rules, slices, and acceptance thresholds before optimizing a language system.

skills.title: Human evaluation and rubric reliability
skills.definition: Train evaluators on anchored rubrics, use blind comparisons, measure agreement, and adjudicate ambiguous cases.

skills.title: Factuality and groundedness measurement
skills.definition: Separate claim correctness, evidence support, citation accuracy, completeness, and calibrated uncertainty.

skills.title: Safety threat models and red teaming
skills.definition: Identify users, assets, misuse cases, failure severity, safeguards, and residual risk; test only in authorized controlled environments.

skills.title: Bias and multilingual evaluation
skills.definition: Evaluate dialects, languages, identities, and culturally dependent meanings with appropriate reviewers and sample-size uncertainty.

skills.title: Privacy and sensitive-data controls
skills.definition: Minimize collection, detect and redact sensitive data, constrain retention, isolate access, and test memorization or disclosure risks.

skills.title: Production monitoring and change control
skills.definition: Track quality, safety, latency, cost, retrieval health, model versions, and prompt versions with staged changes and rollback.

skills.title: Responsible launch and incident response
skills.definition: Launch only with owners, user disclosure, feedback and appeal paths, escalation, containment, recovery, and documented limitations.
